tasks.short: Instruct staff on radiologic techniques, positions and projections

steps.what: Review the actual examination request, relevant patient constraints and approved imaging protocol
inputs: authorized examination request and patient context
outputs: source-checked examination context and applicable protocol

steps.what: Choose the desired technique, patient position and projection for the actual examination
inputs: source-checked examination context and applicable protocol
outputs: radiologist-selected examination technique, position and projections

steps.what: Enter and check the exact patient-specific technique instructions in the examination protocol record
inputs: radiologist-selected examination technique, position and projections
source-checked examination context and applicable protocol

steps.what: Save the checked protocol instruction in the same examination record
Instruct radiologic staff on the desired techniques, positions or projections and resolve actual questions
inputs: staff's actual questions or positioning difficulties
outputs: staff instructed and actual technique questions resolved

tasks.design: Configure a native protocol view in {OPS_SYSTEM} to bring the existing request and applicable protocol together. The radiologist chooses the actual technique, records and checks the patient-specific instruction, then explains it to staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Request details and approved protocols can require separate navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native radiology worklist and protocol views can surface existing sources together.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting positioning and technique to the actual patient and clinical question.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve practical technique questions with radiologic staff.

ambition.what: Improve source access without delegating technique choice.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: radiology systems hold examination requests and protocol instructions; staff still need patient-specific technique decisions and explanation.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the radiology examination and protocol system. Existing request authors and protocol owners produce sources; radiologist produces the patient-specific instruction. This is a recorded examination-protocol scenario.
Native source view first; no generated protocol, hidden send or automatic imaging control. Save is separate from verbal instruction and fully retained at 1%.
Shares are provisional, not measured. Only navigation changes: gross 2 minus 0.3 view upkeep gives 1.7 net. Ordinary instruction checking is inside s3, not an added approval workflow.
unknowns: Current protocol navigation and whether patient-specific instructions are recorded locally
research_questions: Does the native worklist remove repeated navigation without obscuring patient constraints?

already_counted.description: Check actual request and protocol context

approvals.approved_version: complete patient-specific instruction checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if the native worklist already suffices; cautious range below provisional 1.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in continuing education to maintain expertise

steps.what: Select relevant continuing education activities for actual expertise gaps
Participate in the actual education activity, study the material and assess its relevance to practice
Check actual participation evidence and complete the existing professional learning entry
inputs: provider's actual participation evidence or explicit absence
outputs: complete checked learning entry supported by actual evidence

steps.what: Save the checked learning entry in the same learning record
inputs: complete checked learning entry supported by actual evidence

tasks.design: Retain learning and the existing evidence entry in {LMS}. Native course and completion fields already support the small record step in this scenario; no additional automation establishes expertise or saves learning time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professional learning requires attention and judgement about relevance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning records organize participation evidence but do not replace education.
tasks.still_hard: Understand material and decide how it affects clinical practice.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize gaps and critically assess new knowledge.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: continuing education combines actual learning with participation evidence; a learning record does not establish understanding.

assumptions: LMS is the existing professional learning record. Actual participation occurs before evidence entry. The provider supplies evidence; missing evidence is not manufactured from enrollment.
Native course and completion fields are already available. Learning evidence entry and save are split from education; both remain. No separate enrollment or notice process is invented.
Shares are provisional, not measurements. All work retained; gross and net zero. A same-system save has no saving.
unknowns: Whether provider evidence already transfers natively to the professional record
research_questions: Is any actual participation evidence re-keyed, beyond the small native record entry?

already_counted.description: Check actual participation evidence and learning entry

approvals.approved_version: complete evidence-supported learning entry checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual education and existing native participation entry retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in quality improvement and discuss high-error-risk areas

steps.what: Review the actual cases, discrepancy records and source material selected for quality improvement
inputs: authorized actual quality-review cases and discrepancy records
outputs: radiologist's source-checked case review and error-risk questions

steps.what: Participate in quality improvement discussions about high-error-risk areas and practical changes
inputs: radiologist's source-checked case review and error-risk questions
colleagues' actual case interpretations and suggestions
outputs: radiologist's actual quality-review findings and agreed contribution

steps.what: Enter and check the radiologist's actual findings and agreed contribution in the existing case-review record
inputs: radiologist's actual quality-review findings and agreed contribution

steps.what: Save the checked case-review contribution in the same review record

tasks.design: Configure a native quality-review case view in {OPS_SYSTEM} linking existing discrepancy records to the original images and reports. The radiologist reads the evidence, participates in discussion and records the actual contribution; no model assigns fault or invents actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review sources can require repeated navigation between case and discrepancy records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case links and filtered worklists can bring existing review sources together.
tasks.still_hard: Understand why an error risk exists and agree a useful improvement.
tasks.human_edge: Discuss uncertainty and system causes fairly with colleagues.

ambition.what: Improve source access for actual quality review.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: radiology quality review uses actual cases, images and discrepancy records; native links can reduce navigation while discussion and interpretation remain human.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing radiology case and quality-review record. Existing case authors and quality staff produce review inputs; the radiologist supplies actual findings and contribution.

Native linking first. This scenario includes a normal case-review entry, not a new meeting report or a separate organizational quality plan. No colleague labor or duplicated shared action is claimed as saved.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 3 minus 0.5 link upkeep gives 2.5 net. Record authoring and 1% save remain fully retained; checking is ordinary authoring work.
unknowns: Actual navigation burden and local requirement for the radiologist's case-review entry
research_questions: Does a native linked worklist reduce navigation without changing substantive review or exposing inappropriate case data?

already_counted.description: Check actual source cases and discrepancy records

incremental.description: Maintain case-view links and access filters

approvals.approved_version: complete case-review contribution checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native linking already sufficient; cautious range below provisional 2.5% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review the actual indication, imaging, medical context and relevant patient constraints
Determine the appropriate treatment approach, alternatives and patient-specific precautions
outputs: radiologist's patient-specific treatment decisions and limitations

steps.what: Write and finish checking the treatment plan with actual decisions, precautions and existing episode details
inputs: radiologist's patient-specific treatment decisions and limitations
outputs: complete checked patient-specific radiology treatment plan

steps.what: Save the checked treatment plan in the same clinical record
inputs: complete checked patient-specific radiology treatment plan

tasks.design: Configure treatment-plan headings and existing episode identifiers in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The radiologist supplies and checks every clinical decision; the template organizes the plan without choosing treatment or generating orders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-form plan authoring may repeat headings and episode details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical plan templates can reuse those nonclinical fields.
tasks.still_hard: Select a safe, appropriate approach from the actual indication and patient context.
tasks.human_edge: Own treatment decisions and their limitations.

ambition.what: Reduce plan formatting while retaining clinical planning.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5; clinical plan-owner consultation and access approval

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical plan templates can supply headings and identifiers while clinicians determine and check patient-specific treatment content.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the clinical plan record. Existing clinical sources produce facts; radiologist evaluates them in s1 and produces treatment decisions in s2. A plan does not establish treatment delivery.
Native template first. No generated clinical judgement, prescription, order transmission or unmodeled action. Ordinary plan checking remains within authoring; save is separate and fully retained.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 3.4 minus 0.5 template upkeep gives 2.9 net; no saving is assigned to the 1% same-system save.
unknowns: Current plan template and actual repeated formatting burden
research_questions: Can native headings reduce formatting without encouraging default or copied clinical decisions?

already_counted.description: Author and check actual treatment plan

incremental.description: Maintain clinical plan headings and identifier mappings

approvals.approved_version: complete patient-specific plan checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native template already sufficient; cautious range below provisional 2.9% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Radiology administrators can configure existing protocol, case-review and plan views; clinical decisions remain with radiologists.
skills_to_grow: Keep patient constraints visible in native views
Avoid default clinical claims in templates
role.ambitious_version: Improve access to actual clinical sources and reduce repeated plan formatting while retaining instruction, education and clinical judgement.
